# The Lantern Keeper

## One

The lighthouse had not been lit for eleven years, and still the keeper climbed
the stairs every evening at dusk. He carried a brass lamp, a rag, and a book he
had read so many times that the spine had given up.

> A light is a promise you cannot take back.

He set the lamp on the windowsill and opened the book.

## Two

The girl arrived on a Tuesday, soaked through, carrying a paper bag of oranges.

- She did not knock.
- She did not explain.
- She simply sat down and peeled an orange.

He poured tea. They listened to the wind. In the morning she was gone, but the
orange peel was still on the table, coiled like a small yellow rope.

## Three

Some nights he wrote in the logbook:

1. Wind from the north.
2. Lamp cleaned.
3. One visitor, name unknown.

`The logbook is the only honest record`, he thought. Everything else is memory,
and memory edits.

### A note on the text

This story was written for a lighthouse that no longer stands. The keeper is
invented; the oranges are not.

```text
A light is a promise you cannot take back.
```
